VBO:0200620.summary: A working pack scenthound, the Great Anglo-French Tricolor Hound is recorded with roe-deer packs such as Rallye Pic’Antin and boar packs such as La Fond du Loup. Its breed standard describes a solid hound with predominantly French type and a visible Foxhound influence. Working ability remains part of its official classification.
VBO:0200620.shortDescription: A French pack scenthound recorded in both roe-deer and boar hunts, with French type and Foxhound influence.

sources.title: FCI322 — Great Anglo-French Tricolor Hound standard
sources.evidence: Exact valid1983 standard in1996 English translation: solid French-predominant type with Foxhound origin, scenthound with workingtrial; no positive character section. Medium equal skull/muzzle, medium rolled drop ears, strong body, four round feet, tricolor black mantle/bright copper tan without darkoverlay, long well-haired elegantly carried tail; bad curved/deviated tail is fault. No invented sociability/endurance/voice or parent temperament.

VBO:0200621.summary: Friendly, close to people and easy to manage in kennels in its breed standard, the Great Anglo-French White and Black Hound is valued for hunting deer on damp or bushy ground. Its type traces to mid-nineteenth-century crosses between Saintonge hounds and English Foxhounds. Modern packs such as the Equipage de Neubourg continue its roe-deer work.
VBO:0200621.shortDescription: A friendly pack hound in its standard, valued for deer hunts on damp or bushy ground, with Saintonge and Foxhound roots.

VBO:0200622.summary: A working pack scenthound, the Great Anglo-French White and Orange Hound is listed with Rallye Hourvari, a French roe-deer pack, in the Société de Vènerie’s current directory. Its standard keeps working trials within the breed’s official classification. The United Kennel Club recognized this distinct hound in 2006.
VBO:0200622.shortDescription: A French pack scenthound recorded with roe-deer hunters, recognized by the United Kennel Club in 2006.
